milestone: Fastest to ICC No. 1 ODI Batter
details: Reached World No. 1 ODI ranking in just 42 innings.
Appointed India captain for the inaugural 2007 ICC World T20.
Captained India in 3rd Test vs South Africa at Kanpur (India won by 8 wickets).
Led Chennai Super Kings in their inaugural IPL match vs Kings XI Punjab.
Led India to ICC Test Championship Mace No. 1 ranking for the first time.
Player of the Match in World Cup Final with 91*.
Scored 224 vs Australia in Chennai (highest by an Indian wicketkeeper).
First captain in history to win T20 WC (2007), CWC (2011), and Champions Trophy (2013).
Retired from Test cricket after 90 matches, 4876 runs, and 27 wins as captain.
First wicketkeeper in cricket history to effect 100 stumpings in ODIs.
Became only the 2nd wicketkeeper-batsman (after Sangakkara) to reach 10,000 ODI runs with a 50+ career average.
Captained India for the 200th time vs Afghanistan in Asia Cup at Dubai.
Announced retirement from international cricket ('Consider me as retired from 1929 hrs').
Led CSK to record 5th IPL title in his 250th IPL appearance.
